 Live Updates: U.S. launches strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in Strait of Hormuz
 By
 Duarte Dias 
 Duarte Dias 
 Digital Journalist 
 Duarte Pita Dias is based in CBS News' London bureau, where he works across digital platforms and for TV broadcasts.
 Read Full Bio 
 Duarte Dias 
 Updated on: November 17, 2026 / 5:23 PM EST 
 / CBS News
 Add CBS News on Google 
 What to know about the Iran war today:
 The U.S. launched strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, according to an Iranian official. The strikes came hours after Iran said it targeted a U.S. radar system in Bahrain. U.S. Central Command said those attack drones were all intercepted. 
 Iran also claimed Tuesday that another oil tanker was on fire near the Strait of Hormuz after striking a sea mine. Daily claims by the regime of ships hitting mines have not been confirmed, and the U.S. military says the shipping lanes in the southern strait are mine-free and safe to use.
 Vice President JD Vance told Fox News on Monday that the Trump administration won't let the Iran war become a two-year commitment, but he reiterated the White House's justification for launching the war , insisting that Iran's nuclear program remains a threat to the United States.
 New Updates
 48m ago
 Man convicted in Iran-backed plot to murder Trump gets 27.5 years in prison
 A Pakistani man who was convicted of attempted terrorism and orchestrating a murder-for-hire plot at the direction of Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps, with potential targets including President Trump and former President Joe Biden, was sentenced to 27 1/2 years in federal prison on Tuesday.
 Asif Merchant was convicted in March — shortly after the start of the Iran war — on terrorism and murder-for-hire charges and faced up to life in prison. Merchant shuffled into court with a serious expression and shackled ankles, peering around the room. He had wavy gray hair and wore a tan prison outfit. He pressed a headphone to his ear, for an Urdu translation of the proceedings, watching the judge intently and bobbing in his chair as he learned his fate.
 Read more here. 
 By
 Katrina Kaufman, Jacob Rosen

 link copied 
 2:38 PM
 U.S. announces "self-defense" strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island
 The U.S. launched precision strikes on an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps missile site on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to a U.S. military official.
 The official said the strike was launched "in self-defense." 
 "The strike was in response to IRGC aggression targeting U.S. personnel and assets," the official said. "U.S. Central Command remains highly vigilant and fully postured to protect Americans across the region."
 While the official did not specifically mention the IRGC aggression, the strikes came hours after Iran targeted a U.S. radar site in Bahrain. The strikes were successfully intercepted, according to U.S. Central Command. 
 This was the third attempted strike by Iran on a U.S. military installation in the last five days. All of them were intercepted, U.S. officials said.
 Iran had earlier said the U.S. attacked Qeshm Island, but they "caused no damage to residential, commercial, or infrastructural areas," according to Ahmad Nafisi, deputy provincial governor of the southern province of Hormozgan, quoted by the official IRNA news agency.
 An infographic showing Qeshm Island created on Nov. 3, 2026. 
 Omar Zaghloul/Anadolu via Getty Images
 By
 Mark Osborne, Charlie D'Agata 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-4b0f4457 
 link copied 
 2:17 PM
 Iraq resumes pumping oil through pipeline to Turkey in order to avoid Strait of Hormuz
 Iraq has resumed pumping oil to Turkey through a pipeline at an initial capacity of 120,000 barrels a day, Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair al-Abadi said Tuesday in comments carried by state media. The export capacity will be gradually increased to reach 500,000 barrels a day, he said.
 The capacity is fairly small compared to other pipelines in the region. The Saudi East-West pipeline, which crosses from the Persian Gulf to the Red Sea in order to avoid the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb Strait, has a capacity of 7 million barrels per day.
 In August, Iraq and Turkey signed a deal to increase oil exports through a pipeline to the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan.
 Iraq is moving to strengthen the resilience of its oil export infrastructure following the U.S.-Iran war's disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
 The Iraq-Turkey pipeline has been largely idle since 2023 following legal and commercial disputes.
 AP/CBS 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-9a7ef2ed 
 link copied 
 1:52 PM
 Qatar says U.S.-Iran mediation efforts continue
 Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari said Tuesday that mediation efforts between the U.S. and Iran were continuing and a meeting with the Iranian side would be held later in the day to exchange views on proposals under discussion.
 He warned any escalation on the ground posed an "extremely grave danger" to the prospects of reaching an agreement.
 Earlier, President Trump said Iran would "pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before" if it follows through on its reported desire to set off a dirty bomb in Washington, D.C. — a claim denied by Iranian officials .
 Mr. Trump made the remark after being quizzed by reporters about whether there was an imminent threat to Washington from Iran.
 "I hope it's not. But we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy," said Mr. Trump, who was meeting with leaders of Japan, India and Australia in the Philippines.
 AP/CBS 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-cbda60d5 
 link copied 
 1:20 PM
 Houthis say they targeted crucial Saudi East-West oil pipeline in drone attacks
 The Iran-backed Houthi militant group in Yemen said it carried out successful drone strikes Tuesday on the Saudi East-West pipeline.
 Pumping Station No. 9, west of Riyadh, was allegedly targeted in two phases with three one-way attack drones, the Houthis said. They then targeted Pumping Station No. 8 with two drones. The Houthis claimed they made "precise and direct" hits on the pumping stations.
 The Saudis had earlier said they shot down a Houthi drone near Riyadh but it was unclear if it was related to the attack on the East-West pipeline.
 The pipeline, which is comprised of 11 pumping stations, was previously targeted in a drone attack on Sept. 11, which knocked out the line for nearly two weeks. That attack was blamed on Iran-backed rebel groups located in northern Iraq.
 The pipeline gives the Saudis a way to avoid the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb Strait and instead take oil north in the Red Sea out of the Suez Canal. The 750-mile pipeline, built in the 1980s, consists of two separate pipes carrying a maximum capacity of 7 million barrels of oil per day. 
 Infographic with map showing route of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which can transport up to 7 million barrels of oil per day and bypass the chokepoints of Bab-al-Mandab and the Strait of Hormuz. 
 Patricio Arana/AFP via Getty Images
 By
 Mark Osborne 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-0094d925 
 link copied 
 12:46 PM
 Saudis shoot down Houthi drone near Riyadh, coalition says
 The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Iran-backed Houthi militia intercepted and shot down a drone near Riyadh on Tuesday, the spokesperson for the group, Col. Turki Al-Malki, said on X.
 The Houthis have regularly fired one-way attack drones at Riyadh since the civil war in Yemen restarted this summer. The Houthis have been fighting Saudi-backed Yemeni forces aligned with the internationally recognized government.
 This was the fourth straight day the Houthis had fired attack drones into Saudi Arabia, but all of them were intercepted, according to the coalition. The Saudi coalition said it intercepted two drones in the Mecca and Riyadh regions on Monday as well as four separate Houthi drone attacks across the country on Sunday.
 By
 Mark Osborne 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-0796c75e 
 link copied 
 12:10 PM
 U.S.-Israeli war has created "horrific" situation for Iranians, Amnesty International says
 Iranian authorities have intensified their repression of the country's population in response to the Middle East war, which began weeks after their deadly crackdown on anti-government protests killed thousands of people , Amnesty International said on Tuesday.
 An internet blackout imposed at the time of the crackdown on Jan. 8 and 9 and the scale of the casualties meant it was not yet possible for the group to quantify the number of people killed, Amnesty's lead Iran researcher, Raha Bahreini, said.
 But she told AFP in an interview that "there is no doubt that thousands were massacred in less than 48 hours."
 She added that the Middle East war, which began with U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb. 28, "with Iranians still reeling from the January massacres, created a horrific situation for the people in the country."
 "The authorities used the cover of wartime conditions to intensify repression," she said.
 Bahreini lamented the international community had shifted its attention away from the Iranian people to the geopolitical consequences of the conflict.
 "The massacres that took place in January, which should have moved then global consciousness, have faded away from attention," she said.
 By
 AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-f24a7175 
 link copied 
 11:46 AM
 Iran's foreign minister refers to dirty bomb report as "RUBBISH"
 Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi slammed reports that his country was targeting Washington, D.C., with chemical weapons or building missiles under dams, blaming the reports on Israel. 
 "In the past 72 hours, pro-Israel media have 'reported' that Iran is supposedly plotting to use chemical weapons in DC while building missile bases under dams. RUBBISH," Araghchi wrote on X .
 CNN reported that Iran could be developing plans to target administration officials with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington. According to sources cited by CNN, Tehran's planning is, for now, "an effort to give itself options rather than an indicator of an imminent attack."
 Separately, The New York Times reported that Iran's network of dams might be cover for underground missile development. 
 In his social media post, Araghchi also invoked the misguided U.S. assertion of there being weapons of mass destruction in Iraq as cause for invading that country in 2003 .
 "Spare us the Iraq War-style propaganda, especially with Israeli fingerprints all over it," Araghchi said Tuesday. "Nobody is buying it."
 Araghchi has been one of the most important members of negotiations between the U.S. and Iran over a lasting peace deal.  
 By
 Mark Osborne 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-89f19eee 
 link copied 
 11:04 AM
 U.S. strikes Iran's Qeshm Island in Strait of Hormuz, Iranian official says
 The United States on Tuesday carried out several attacks on Iran's southern island of Qeshm, located in the Strait of Hormuz, a local Iranian official said.
 "The American attack on locations on Qeshm island caused no damage to residential, commercial, or infrastructural areas," said Ahmad Nafisi, deputy provincial governor of the southern province of Hormozgan, quoted by the official IRNA news agency.
 There was no immediate confirmation of an attack by the United States.
 Qeshm Island has been a regular target of strikes by the U.S. throughout the war. Most of them have been categorized as "defensive" attacks targeting drone or missile launch equipment. The U.S. acknowledged Iran fired multiple one-way attack drones toward Bahrain, but said they were all shot down.
 CBS/AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-41529903 
 link copied 
 10:24 AM
 Iran-backed group warns it will fight Iraqi forces entering its stronghold
 A powerful Iran-backed armed group in Iraq vowed on Tuesday to confront government forces if they try to enter its main stronghold near Baghdad, denying allegations it is smuggling oil from the area.
 The standoff between Kataib Hezbollah and Iraqi authorities is shaping up to be the first major test of the new government's resolve to disarm nonstate armed groups.
 Abu Taleb al-Saidi of Kataib Hezbollah made the comments a day after Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said security forces would enter Jurf al-Sakhar, south of Baghdad in Babil province, later this week. Local media reported the group had until Friday to leave.
 Kataib Hezbollah, one of Iraq's most powerful armed groups, wields considerable influence in Jurf al-Sakhar and has maintained an armed presence there for more than a decade.
 The planned move by al-Zaidi is part of his push to disarm powerful Iran-backed groups by mid-2027. The move by the rival sides raises alarms of internal Shiite fighting that has been mostly avoided since the 2003 U.S.-led invasion that removed Saddam Hussein from power.
 By
 The Associated Press 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-63dd93d9 
 link copied 
 9:33 AM
 Iranian navy claims 3 oil tankers have hit sea mines near Strait of Hormuz today alone
 Iran's navy claimed a third oil tanker struck a sea mine near the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday after trying to use shipping lanes declared safe and open by the United States, but which Iranian authorities have repeatedly warned mariners against using.
 The semi-official Fars news agency cited the Iranian Army Navy as saying the third "offending" tanker "caught fire after striking a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz."
 "Our message is clear: the Strait of Hormuz is closed. Safe passage requires coordination with the Iranian Armed Forces, transit through designated safe zones, and having navigation systems switched on," the Fars report cited the navy as saying.
 Iran has made claims of ships striking sea mines in and around the southern Strait of Hormuz for weeks, without offering evidence. Independent monitoring agencies report frequent, unexplained explosions impacting vessels in the region, but the commander of the U.S. military's Central Command declared the strait's southern shipping lanes completely de-mined and safe to navigate as recently as late October.
 By
 Tucker Reals 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-e21ad4cf 
 link copied 
 8:59 AM
 Iran's Houthi allies say key Bab el-Mandeb Strait shipping lanes "safer now" in their hands
 Iran's Houthi allies said Tuesday that the shipping lanes of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the southern gateway to the Red Sea that provides access to Saudi Arabia's oil and gas export hub of Yanbu Port, are "safer now" after they seized control of Yemen's coastline on the waterway from Saudi-backed forces.
 The Iran-backed rebel group has fought Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces for control of the strait for months, and the declaration by their spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree on Tuesday came a day after a government-allied group said its fighters had retreated from areas along the Yemeni coastline near the strait amid relentless Houthi attacks. 
 Fighting between the Saudi-led coalition that backs Yemen's government and the Houthis has escalated this year, putting control of the vital sea passage at stake as Iran and the U.S. attempt to exert control over the nearby Strait of Hormuz. 
 A map shows major routes for energy resources and other trade from the Middle East to Asia, including the Bab el-Mandeb strait and the Strait of Hormuz. 
 Getty/iStockphoto
 Saudi Arabia has attempted to impose a naval blockade of Houthi-held territory in Yemen, and the Houthis have responded by declaring their own blockade of Saudi ports and vessels in the Red Sea, launching several attacks on ships.
 Almost a third of global oil supplies would typically transit both straits before the U.S. and Israel launched their war on Iran, and while shipments via the Strait of Hormuz have rebounded, the unresolved, interlinked conflicts have kept risks for shipping companies high, which in turn has kept global oil prices up about 40% compared to before the war.
 A map from the U.K. navy's Maritime Trade Operations center shows incidents involving commercial vessels in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz, and in the Gulf of Aden near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, in the weeks leading up to Nov. 12, 2026. 
 UKMTO / ©2026 OSM ©2026 TomTom ©2026 EarthStar Geographics
 "We will continue our military operations deep into Saudi territory, responding to the blockade with a blockade and to escalation with escalation, and targeting the Saudi enemy's military buildup and its officers until the aggression ceases and the blockade against our beloved people is lifted," Saree said in his Tuesday statement, adding that the group, "also assure the world that navigation through the Bab al-Mandab Strait is safer now that the Saudi enemy has been defeated and its forces have been dispersed."   
 By
 Tucker Reals 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-c2b3558a 
 link copied 
 8:18 AM
 Iran dismisses CNN report on possible chemical weapon plot against Washington
 Iran on Tuesday dismissed as baseless a CNN report suggesting it was preparing to launch a possible chemical "dirty bomb" attack on Washington, D.C. 
 "Those who initiated the aggression against Iran are now seeking to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs by manufacturing and disseminating baseless allegations, including the recent claims published by The New York Times and the fabricated media narrative surrounding an alleged 'dirty bomb' propagated by CNN," Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said in a post on X. 
 CBS/AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-e2c3f43a 
 link copied 
 7:41 AM
 U.S. says 3rd Iranian attack on Bahrain radar installation in less than a week was intercepted
 The U.S. military's Central Command said Tuesday that Iran's third claimed attack targeting a U.S. radar installation in Bahrain was thwarted by air defense systems.
 "Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed its drones hit a U.S. military radar system at a base in Bahrain early this morning. This is FALSE," CENTCOM said in a statement shared on social media. 
 It acknowledged that Iran had launched the attack on Tuesday, however, saying "multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the IRGC today towards Bahrain were intercepted without any damage to U.S. equipment or injury to American personnel."
 Iran issued nearly identical claims to have struck a U.S. radar site on a military base in Bahrain on Friday and Sunday, all of which were intercepted according to American and Bahraini authorities. 
 The incidents appear to represent an increase in attempted strikes by Iran against U.S. interests and infrastructure across the Persian Gulf region. Large-scale tit-for-tat strikes largely ended over the summer, with the war grinding into a stalemate as both Iran and the U.S. refuse to back down from their demands for a peace deal.
 President Trump has suggested an agreement may not be necessary and that the status quo could be acceptable, despite ongoing threats to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz keeping global oil prices about 40% higher than they were before the war, and no agreement to renew international monitoring of Iran's opaque nuclear program.
 By
 Tucker Reals 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-02405c98 
 link copied 
 7:15 AM
 Trump says he's taking report of possible Iranian chemical bomb plot "very seriously"
 President Trump said Tuesday that he is taking "very seriously" a CNN report suggesting Iran may be plotting to attack Washington with a chemical weapon.
 According to sources cited by CNN, Tehran could be developing plans to target administration officials in the U.S. capital with a so-called dirty bomb. The sources cited said the planning was not an indicator of an imminent attack, but an effort to explore options.
 Arriving in the Philippines Tuesday, Mr. Trump told reporters that "if there is" such a plot, Iran "will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before." 
 "I hope it's not," he said. "But we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy."
 Asked earlier about the report, White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said the administration remained vigilant in "monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland."
 CBS/AP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-0d4ae4e7 
 link copied 
 6:04 AM
 Qatar calls for restraint after Iran claims attack on U.S. radar in Bahrain
 Qatar on Tuesday called for "all parties" to avoid a new escalation Tuesday after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed for the third time in less than a week to have targeted a U.S. radar system in Bahrain.
 "We call on all parties to exercise restraint during this period and to avoid any escalation that could undermine negotiation efforts," Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari said at a press briefing in Doha, warning of an "extremely serious" threat to efforts to forge an agreement to end the Mideast war.
 President Trump has kept his intentions on Iran ambiguous, repeatedly insisting that the war has been won and he no longer considers it necessary to make a deal with the Islamic Republic, but also keeping the possibility of renewed U.S. attacks on the table. 
 CBS/AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-12d164a8 
 link copied 
 5:31 AM
 Iran claims another oil tanker hit a sea mine near Strait of Hormuz
 Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed Tuesday that another oil tanker had struck a sea mine and was on fire near the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency, which is closely linked with the IRGC.
 "A short while ago, an offending oil tanker — which was navigating within a restricted zone east of the Strait of Hormuz with its navigation systems switched off and in violation of established regulations — caught fire and sustained severe damage after striking a naval mine," the report said, citing the IRGC. 
 Iranian forces have claimed similar incidents on a nearly daily basis for weeks, though it has offered no evidence. Independent maritime monitors report frequent explosions, caused by unknown projectiles, impacting ships in the region.
 Tehran has repeatedly warned ships not to use southern routes through the Strait of Hormuz, close to Oman's coast, that the U.S. military insists are de-mined and safe to navigate. Iran demands that all vessels seek permission to use a northern passage close to its own shores, and it has attacked ships that use the southern route with missiles and drones since the summer.
 By
 Duarte Dias 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-a609a9d2 
 link copied 
 4:47 AM
 Iranian and Omani ministers discuss Strait of Hormuz options
 The Iranian and Omani foreign ministers discussed "safeguarding" shipping and diplomatic options, Oman's official news agency said on Tuesday.
 Iran's top diplomat, Abbas Araghchi, and his Omani counterpart Badr Albusaidi held talks in the Omani capital, Muscat, on the "diplomatic options available to contain tensions and revitalise tracks of dialogue and negotiation," according to the agency.
 "These efforts aim to expand areas of mutual understanding among the concerned parties and prevent the widening of the crisis and its repercussions," it added.
 Iran and Oman's coastline form the Strait of Hormuz, and the two countries were engaged in talks on the potential future management of the waterway in recent months.
 CBS/AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-1d002ff2 
 link copied 
 3:49 AM
 Iran claims another attack on U.S. radar systems in Bahrain
 Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corp said Tuesday it targeted U.S. radar systems in Bahrain for the third time since Friday.
 "Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain," the Guards' Sepah news website said, adding that the attack was in response to the "repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones."
 Bahrain issued an alert Tuesday morning, urging residents to seek shelter and to remain calm, before giving the all clear shortly after. Explosions were heard over the Bahraini capital of Manama on Tuesday.
 CBS/AFP 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-263e27e3 
 link copied 
 2:33 AM
 White House downplays Iranian dirty bomb plot report
 A White House official has downplayed a CNN report suggesting that Iran could be developing plans to target administration officials with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington.
 According to sources cited by CNN,  Tehran's planning is, for now, "an effort to give itself options rather than an indicator of an imminent attack."
 In response to the report, White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said, "We remain vigilant monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland."
 By
 Duarte Dias 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-5b3edd34 
 link copied 
 9:13 PM
 Vance says there's "no daylight" between him and Trump on war with Iran
 In an interview with Fox News that aired Monday night, Vice President JD Vance said "there's no daylight" between himself and President Trump, after he was asked about his post-election comments on the war with Iran being the reason for GOP midterm defeats .
 "I think there's no daylight between the president or any other senior member of the administration," Vance told Laura Ingraham.
 Vance also said that neither he nor the president want the conflict to become a forever war.
 "... We have accomplished an extraordinary amount. We have destroyed the nuclear program. We have destroyed Iran's conventional military," Vance said. "... The President of the United States has a lot of options, right? He could say, 'We're done now.' He could of course, exert more military and diplomatic pressure on the Iranians. I think it's something he's thinking about doing right now, right? What are we actually going to do to finally bring this thing to a resolution?"
 Vance positioned himself as a skeptic of foreign military entanglements before he became vice president, and early in the Iran war, Mr. Trump conceded that Vance was "philosophically, a little bit different than me" and "less enthusiastic about going." Still, Vance has publicly stood by the president on the Iran war, and helped lead a U.S.-Iran diplomatic push over the summer.
 By
 Kiki Intarasuwan 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-dc4d4b7f 
 link copied 
 5:59 PM / November 16, 2026
 Another tanker hits naval mine in Strait of Hormuz, Iranian officials say
 A tanker struck a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday and caught fire, according to Iranian state media.
 It is the fourth such incident in 24 hours, the Islamic Republic of Iran Navy told semi-official news agency ISNA in a statement. Officials did not identify the vessel or provide further information.
 Meanwhile, a British maritime agency on Monday said it received a third-party report of an attack involving a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz, just north of Khasab, Oman. The incident disabled the vessel and resulted in an engine room fire, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations.
 "The crew have been reported safe. Damage assessment, and environmental impact are unknown at the time of this report," the UKMTO said.
 By
 Kiki Intarasuwan 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-89740f02 
 link copied 
 4:14 PM / November 16, 2026
 Vance says U.S. won't let Iran war become 2-year commitment
 Vice President JD Vance told Fox News that the Trump administration won't let the Iran war become a two-year commitment. He also said the Iranian nuclear program was still a threat to the U.S.
 "We told the American people we would do no more forever wars. Yes, the president felt he had to destroy the nuclear program, and, yes, the Iranian nuclear program is a threat to the United States of America," Vance told Fox News' Laura Ingraham in a clip from an interview expected to air Monday night. "But we are not going to allow this to become a 10- or 15-year commitment or, frankly, even a two-year commitment."
 The U.S. and Israel started the war at the end of February. Throughout the conflict, President Trump has said that Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon. The Iranian regime has maintained for years that its nuclear program is for peaceful purposes.
 "Despite the fact that a lot of neoconservatives and a lot of other people want us to stay there forever, we're not going to stay there forever," Vance told Ingraham. "We promised we wouldn't, and I have full confidence the president will get us out of this thing with great results."
 By
 Alex Sundby 
 https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-nuclear-oil-strait-of-hormuz/#post-update-96dbce7a 
 link copied 
 2:48 PM / November 16, 2026
 U.S. Central Command posts photo of newest carrier in Middle East
 U.S. Central Command posted on Monday a photo of the newest aircraft carrier operating in the Middle East, the USS Theodore Roosevelt.
 A U.S. military official confirmed to CBS News senior national security correspondent Charlie D'Agata on Sunday that the Roosevelt had joined the two other carriers in the region, the USS George H.W. Bush and the USS George Washington.
 The USS Theodore Roosevelt moves through the Indian Ocean, Nov. 15, 2026, in a photo posted by U.S. Central Command. 
 U.S. Central Command
 Central Command said the Roosevelt was in its area of responsibility as part of a scheduled deployment.
 The three ships aren't all expected to remain in the area for long as carrier strike groups rotate through the region.
 By
